description: We are DevVerse, a multidisciplinary team combining Research, GIS & Geospatial Analysis, SAR & Remote Sensing, Data Analytics, UI/UX Design, and Full-Stack Development. We transform complex satellite and Earth observation data into meaningful insights and interactive web solutions.
summary:
"7Echo" is an interactive earthquake analysis platform developed by Team "DevVerse" to investigate the impacts of the 7.7-magnitude Myanmar earthquake that struck on March 28, 2025, along the Sagaing Fault.

The platform integrates Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite imagery, earthquake data, and geospatial information to explore earthquake-related surface deformation and landscape changes. Through interactive maps, pre- and post-earthquake comparisons, and data visualizations, users can investigate affected areas and better understand the relationship between fault movements and surface changes.

7Echo addresses the challenge by demonstrating how satellite-based Earth observation and GIS technologies can transform complex scientific data into accessible insights for earthquake research and disaster assessment. This project is important because it highlights the value of NASA and other satellite resources in understanding geological hazards, supporting scientific research, and improving disaster awareness in Myanmar and beyond.
details:
1. What does the project do and how does it work?

“7Echo” is an interactive Earth observation and earthquake analysis platform designed to explore the impacts of the 7.7-magnitude Myanmar earthquake that occurred on March 28, 2025, along the Sagaing Fault.

The platform uses Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite observations, earthquake information, and geospatial datasets to help users investigate changes in the Earth's surface associated with seismic activity.

It brings together satellite imagery, geographic information, and earthquake-related data in an interactive web application. Users can explore earthquake locations, examine the Sagaing Fault region, visualize satellite observations, and compare available pre- and post-earthquake datasets to better understand surface changes.

The platform aims to make complex remote sensing and geological information easier to explore and understand through interactive maps, visualizations, and accessible explanations.

2. What benefits does the project have?

Earthquake Awareness: Helps users understand the geographical impact of the Myanmar earthquake.

Satellite Data Accessibility: Makes Earth observation and SAR-related information easier to explore.

Geospatial Understanding: Connects earthquake locations, fault systems, and geographical information.

Scientific Learning: Introduces users to SAR technology and its applications in earthquake research.

Data Visualization: Transforms complex scientific datasets into understandable visual information.

Disaster Assessment Support: Demonstrates how satellite observations can contribute to understanding earthquake-affected regions.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our goal is to bridge the gap between complex satellite observations and public understanding of earthquake impacts.

By focusing on the 2025 Myanmar earthquake, “7Echo” demonstrates how Earth observation technology can help researchers, students, educators, and interested communities explore geological changes and understand the importance of satellite-based disaster monitoring.

In the long term, we hope to expand the platform to support the exploration of other earthquakes and natural hazards in Myanmar and around the world.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Our team used a combination of programming technologies, geospatial tools, satellite data resources, design software, and AI-powered tools to research, develop, and implement "7Echo".

Programming Languages

  • Python
  • TypeScript

Frameworks and Libraries

  • React
  • Tailwind CSS 
  • GeoPandas
  • Pandas
  • NumPy
  • Leaflet

Satellite Data and Research Resources

  • NASA Earth observation resources
  • ASF DAAC (Alaska Satellite Facility)
  • Sentinel-1 SAR imagery
  • NISAR mission documentation and resources
  • Earthquake catalog and geological datasets

  • Google Earth Pro 
  • Visual Studio Code
  • GitHub

Deployment

  • CloudFlare DNS

Hardware

  • Laptops
  • Internet Connection & Wifi

5. How is the project creative?

The creativity of “7Echo” comes from transforming complex radar satellite observations into an interactive storytelling and exploration experience. Instead of presenting satellite imagery as isolated scientific data, our platform connects three important perspectives:

  • Earthquake Events: Understanding when and where seismic activity occurred.
  • Earth Observation: Exploring how SAR satellite technology can detect changes in the Earth's surface.
  • Geological Storytelling: Connecting observed changes with the Sagaing Fault and the broader geological context of Myanmar.

The concept of "7Echo" represents the interaction between satellite radar observations and the dynamic movement of the Earth. It combines science, technology, visualization, and storytelling to make remote sensing more engaging and accessible.

6. What factors did our team consider?

During development, Team DevVerse considered several important factors:

  • Scientific Accuracy: Distinguishing actual satellite observations from assumptions and interpretations.
  • Data Reliability: Using credible satellite, earthquake, and geological data sources.
  • Geospatial Accuracy: Considering coordinate systems, map projections, geographic boundaries, and data resolution.
  • Before-and-After Comparison: Ensuring that satellite observations are suitable for meaningful temporal comparison.
  • Accessibility: Designing an understandable interface for both technical and non-technical users.
  • Performance: Making satellite imagery and interactive maps efficient to explore.
  • Language Accessibility: Supporting English and Myanmar languages to make the platform more inclusive.
  • Limitations: Recognizing that SAR observations can be affected by vegetation, atmospheric conditions, terrain, and processing methods.
